body.statement: Almost surely, the constrained and unconstrained GCM slopes differ only on a finite contact interval at every \(x\), the integral \(D(x)\) is finite and nonnegative, and \(D\) has a separable locally bounded stationary version. Moreover, the joint contact radius for all \(x\) in a bounded interval has a tail sufficient for independent truncation of well-separated Brownian blocks.
body.justification: The continuum maximum and any declustering rule are meaningful only after the nonlocal GCM energy is localized and given a separable version.
body.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) prove the one-point LR integral is well defined; the uniform contact-radius and local-boundedness statement for the translated field is not supplied there.
body.consumer: It licenses finite-window simulation, block separation, and fine-grid approximation for the canonical calibration.

obligation.what_is_open: A quantitative common contact-radius tail, together with a proved locally bounded separable version of the translated LR field, remains unavailable.
obligation.obstruction: Parabolic drift and Brownian increment stationarity localize any fixed variational picture heuristically, but they do not by themselves control all one-sided constrained and unconstrained GCM touchpoints uniformly over a continuum of constraint locations. The phrase ``tail sufficient for independent truncation'' also lacks a numerical bound to prove.
obligation.attempted: Brownian translation and affine GCM equivariance give exact finite-dimensional stationarity. Attempts to dominate the common contact radius only by the argmin of Brownian motion plus a parabola leave unproved the remote supporting-chord events for the two one-sided GCMs.
obligation.partial_result:
Whenever the two GCM energies are well defined, their stationarity follows exactly rather than asymptotically.  For every \(x,t\in\mathbb R\), set \(\mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x)\).  Then
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Affine equivariance of greatest convex minorants and the change of variable \(s=x+t\) therefore give
\[
 D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained Brownian--GCM energy.  The joint law of \((\mathbb W_{x_1+h},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m+h})\) equals that of \((\mathbb W_{x_1},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m})\) for every \(h\), by stationary Brownian increments.  Hence all finite-dimensional distributions of \(D\) are translation invariant.  This identity does not by itself prove a common finite contact radius, local boundedness, separability, or a quantitative radius tail.
